result.title: Verifying Human-Written Reasoning References
result.summary: Evaluating the reasoning of AI systems often relies on human-written reasoning chains as references, yet the logical support for their individual steps is rarely verified. Although prior neuro-symbolic approaches have formalized and checked reasoning, their reported evaluations do not systematically assess whether step conclusions in human-written reference derivations are entailed by their cited premise sets or investigate the sources of failures in those references. To address these limitations, we present a novel reference-centred assessment method for human-written derivations that combines entailment checking against cited premise sets, full-premise rechecking, and failure attribution to examine the reliability of these derivations and their formal representations. We evaluate it on P-FOLIO, using a large language model (LLM) to translate step conclusions into first-order logic (FOL) and the Z3 SMT solver to check entailment. Of 386 derivations examined, 202 (52.3%) meet all our checking criteria, meaning that every translated step is entailed by its stated support and the required target is established under the available FOL representations. Among 230 steps not entailed by their stated support, 191 become entailed when checked against the complete original premises, indicating that most initial failures reflect incomplete or mismatched support rather than unsupported claims. Manual analysis of the remaining 39 cases identifies 21 human reasoning errors, 11 FOL translation errors, and 7 dataset annotation errors. A separate manual audit of 50 randomly sampled steps that passed the entailment checks found 46 faithful FOL translations (92%). These findings suggest that disagreement with a human-written reasoning reference may originate in the reference or its formal representation rather than in the AI system being evaluated.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出以人类参考推理链为中心的评价方法：用 LLM 将各步结论翻译为一阶逻辑、由 Z3 检查是否被所述前提蕴含，并配合全前提复查与失败归因，在 P-FOLIO 上核查 386 条推导，发现多数初始失败源于支持不完整或错配而非无依据。
AI.relevance_reason: 其步骤级蕴含检查加失败归因（区分人类推理错误、形式化翻译错误、标注错误）的流程，可能为 LVR 中推理步骤监督、以及「错误源自模型还是参考表示」的溯源提供可核查线索，迁移性需人工判断。
